grafite.note: The page ground. Neutral near-black with no hue cast — the replacement for the retired navy ground.

couro.note: The one tonal lift: the trial section and the desktop panel interior.

elev.note: Declared in :root as the next step up the grey ramp. No element paints with it in the shipped build.

campo.note: Input and select interiors only. One step off the ground so the field reads as a recess.

osso.note: All headings and all primary text. Warm-white, not white.

gold.note: The only colour that ever fills an action. Taken from the logo asset's own brass gradient, the single fixed brand colour.

gold-light.note: Brass button hover, the H1's emphasised span, the skip link, and the focus ring. The light end of the logo gradient.

gold-deep.note: Scrollbar thumb on hover and the midpoint of the logo asset's brass gradient (#8f7456 to #a27947 to #e2ca97). Never a surface or text colour.

poste-r.note: Identifier, not an accent. One pole stripe, and the 3px top edge of the profile card for shops that already run a system. Never fills an action.

poste-a.note: Identifier, not an accent. The other pole stripe, and the 3px top edge of the profile card for shops with no system yet. Never fills an action.

wash.note: The neutral tint that lifts a card off the ground. Cards, module tiles and toggle chips. Footer rows use the 20% step.

line.note: Brass at 16% alpha over graphite. Every default border and every section rule — the one place warmth touches a neutral ground.

line-2.note: The raised border. Hover states, the secondary button at rest, the toggle track, the desktop panel frame.

white.note: Declared in :root and held in reserve. No element paints with it in the shipped build.

error.note: Validation only: invalid field borders and their message.

whatsapp.note: Brand value, glyph only. Never text, never a surface.

bella-rose.note: Identifies the sibling product CS Bella in the footer. Never used for CS Barber content.

display.purpose: The H1 only. Two lines, left-aligned, indented 30px to clear the pole, one emphasised span in Lit Brass.

headline.purpose: Section H2s. One per section, standing alone with no eyebrow above it.

title.purpose: Item headings inside lists: module rows, steps, differentiators.

lede.purpose: The hero's supporting paragraph, capped at 52ch.

fact.purpose: The four hero facts over Dim Grey captions. A short noun, never an invented metric.

body.purpose: Document default. Light weight carries all reading copy.

body-small.purpose: List and FAQ prose, capped 48-68ch per component.

label.purpose: Form field labels and fieldset legends, uppercase in Dim Grey.

tier-label.purpose: The two tier markers inside the module block. Lives below a heading, never above one.

wordmark.purpose: CS BARBER in the header. The widest tracking in the system.

action.purpose: Button labels. The only place weight 600 appears outside the wordmark.

gradients.name: poste
gradients.purpose: The barber pole's stripe. Fills the 9px bar beside the H1 at background-size 100% 180%, and nothing else. Brief-pinned: the user named the barber pole as the direction.

gradients.name: caret
gradients.purpose: The select caret's two 5x5px triangles. A drawn shape, not a fill.

gradients.name: foto-scrim
gradients.purpose: Declared over the barbershop photograph to sink its base into the ground. See defects: its ::after ships an empty content declaration, so it does not render today.

shadows.name: button-seat
shadows.purpose: On the brass button only, seating bright paint against the dark ground. Removed when disabled.

shadows.name: pole-seat
shadows.purpose: The pole's inset graphite hairline plus a contact darkening, so the bar reads as an object in front of the page.

shadows.name: photo-contact
shadows.purpose: Under the barbershop photograph in the overlap composition.

shadows.name: panel-contact
shadows.purpose: Under the desktop panel that overhangs the photograph.

shadows.name: phone-contact
shadows.purpose: Under the phone panel, the topmost layer of the overlap.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve for state and reveal. Every transition uses it.

motion.name: poste
motion.purpose: The pole's stripe travelling upward: @keyframes poste animates background-position to 0 -180%. Linear, because a barber pole does not ease. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reveal-opacity
motion.purpose: The fade half of the scroll reveal.

motion.name: reveal-transform
motion.purpose: The 14px rise half of the scroll reveal.

motion.name: reveal-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-element delay inside a revealed section, authored inline as --i (typically 0 to 3).

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and border-colour state changes on links, fields and chips.

motion.name: state-button
motion.purpose: Button background, border and colour transitions.

motion.name: surface
motion.purpose: Header border and background shift on scroll; card border on hover.

motion.name: menu
motion.purpose: The mobile menu panel sliding down from under the header.

motion.name: accordion
motion.purpose: FAQ answer open and close, scripted from measured height.

motion.name: foto-straighten
motion.purpose: The composition photograph rotating from 1.2deg to 0 on hover.

breakpoints.name: stack-break
breakpoints.note: max-width. Hero actions, form grid and toggle chips collapse to one column; the pole narrows to 7px and the headline indent to 22px; the overlap composition caps at 22rem.

breakpoints.name: pair
breakpoints.note: min-width. Profile pair goes two-up, audience cards three-up, fact strip four-up.

breakpoints.name: header-switch
breakpoints.note: max-width. Desktop nav and header CTA hide; the hamburger and slide-down menu take over.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.note: min-width. Differentiators, trial section, footer links and the module base list all split into columns.

browserChrome.name: selection
browserChrome.purpose: Selected text is brass on graphite, not the UA default blue.

browserChrome.name: caret
browserChrome.purpose: The text cursor in every field is brass.

browserChrome.name: focus-ring
browserChrome.purpose: The one focus treatment, keyboard-only, in Lit Brass.

browserChrome.name: underline-offset
browserChrome.purpose: Focused links and summaries get breathing room under the underline.

browserChrome.name: scrollbar
browserChrome.purpose: Graphite track, Deep Brass thumb in Firefox; the WebKit thumb still ships a leftover navy (see defects).

defectsNotCanonized.note: The retired navy. Mobile browser chrome still paints the old ground. Not a token; not inherited by new surfaces.
Navy left over from the previous ramp. The focus signal in this system is the brass border; the interior shift is not recorded as a rule or a token.
Navy thumb left over from the previous ramp. Not a token.
Cool navy-grey placeholder, off the current neutral ramp. Not a token.
Empty content declaration: the ::after never generates, so the photograph's scrim does not render. A live CSS bug, not a design decision.

Detector flag gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow. The user pinned this composition to match the previous site and the shadows are already far shorter than the original's. Left as is, recorded as a pinned exception rather than a system pattern.

narrative.overview:
A barbershop reads as a barbershop from across the street because of two things: the brass on the fittings and the striped pole turning by the door. This system is built from exactly those two and nothing else. The ground is graphite — a neutral near-black with no colour cast at all — and the text is bone. Against that grey quiet, brass is the only colour that can be acted on, and the pole appears once, beside the headline, as the page's single authored moment.

The palette was rebuilt from the one fixed brand fact: the logo asset's brass gradient. Brass is the company's; the previous navy ramp was not, and navy is what made the page read as generic category SaaS. Removing it left a ground with no hue to compete with brass, which is the whole reason the three-colour risk of a barber pole is survivable here. Red and blue are identifiers, not palette: they stripe the pole and they mark two profile cards, and they are forbidden from touching an action.

Everything else is the category convention executed straight — fixed header, left-aligned hero, two-tier module block, numbered implantation sequence, accordion, form — and the discipline is in refusing the signals the category reaches for: no surface gradients, no glow, no card lift, no stock iconography, no second action colour. One typeface at one light weight carries the body; headings step up one notch and never further. Sections breathe on a clamped rhythm that never falls below 64px.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral graphite ground with bone text; no hue in the neutrals at all
Brass is the only colour that fills an action, by rule
The barber pole: one animated striped bar beside the H1, and two 3px card edges — nothing else
Flat surfaces, one-pixel brass hairlines, no gradient fills
Poppins alone: body at 300, headings at 500, actions at 600
Hairline-opened sections on a clamped vertical rhythm
Motion is two gestures: the pole's slow travel, and a staggered rise-and-fade on scroll

rules.name: The Brass Acts Alone Rule
rules.body: Brass is the only colour that ever fills an action. Red and blue never fill a button, never carry a link, never underline text and never appear in a hover state. They exist in exactly two places — the pole beside the H1 and the 3px identifier edge on each of the two profile cards — and that is the complete inventory. The moment a third strong colour starts competing for the eye, brass stops reading as the thing to press, and the palette stops working.

rules.name: The Neutral Ground Rule
rules.body: The greys carry no hue. Ground, surface, field and wash are all neutral, deliberately, so that brass and the pole are the only chroma on the page. A new surface tints with the wash over graphite; it does not get a colour of its own.

rules.name: The Warm Hairline Rule
rules.body: Dividers are brass at 16% alpha, never neutral grey and never solid. A new divider inherits the hairline token; raising a border to the bright hairline is a state change (hover, inset), not a decoration.

rules.name: The No Surface Gradient Rule
rules.body: No surface in this system is filled with a gradient. Three gradients exist and each one draws a shape, not a fill: the pole's repeating stripe, the select caret's two 5x5px triangles, and the scrim over the barbershop photograph. Flat paint everywhere else.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Poppins is the only family. No display face, no mono, no serif, and no system font stack reached for as a shortcut. A new surface that needs a different voice gets it from weight (300 / 500 / 600) and tracking.

rules.name: The Naked Heading Rule
rules.body: A section heading stands alone. No eyebrow, no kicker, no ordinal and no coloured rule sits above an H2 — the heading carries its own weight. Ordinals appear only in the four implantation steps, where the sequence is the information. An uppercase tier label is legal inside a block, placed below the heading to divide a list; it is never promoted to sit above one. The pole is attached to the H1 itself, beside it and spanning its height — it is not an ornament sitting above a heading, and it does not repeat on H2s.

rules.name: The Light Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy is weight 300. Emphasis inside it goes to 500 and Bone, never to 700. Functional text never drops below 11.5px.

rules.name: The Hairline Opens Rule
rules.body: Every section but the first opens with a one-pixel hairline rule across the column. It is the page's only section separator; do not add a background change, a spacer graphic or a decorative divider to do the same job. The pole's stripe does not belong on a section rule — it was tried there as a 56px segment, read as a dashed grey line, and was removed.

rules.name: The One Gesture Rule
rules.body: Apart from the pole, scroll motion is a 14px rise with a fade, staggered by --i. No parallax, no scale, no lateral slide, and nothing animates more than once.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Cards, tiles, inputs and list rows have no shadow at any state. If a new surface needs to separate from the ground, it gets a hairline and a wash — not elevation.

rules.name: The Contact-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow is permitted only where something physically overlaps something else, and only as a negative-spread contact darkening. A shadow that reads as a glow, a drop or a hard offset does not belong in this world.

rules.name: The Two Radius Rule
rules.body: 6px if the user acts on it, 10px if it holds content. Do not introduce a third radius for a new component; decide which side it is on. The pole, the focus ring and the composition's nested frames are the named exceptions and they do not extend.

rules.name: The Drawn Mark Rule
rules.body: Chevrons, carets and arrows are drawn in CSS or as inline SVG in the sprite. No icon font, no glyph character, no emoji, no bitmap, no third-party icon package — the page makes zero external requests and the marks are part of that commitment.

dos: Do let brass be the only colour that fills an action, everywhere, without exception.
Do keep red and blue to the pole and the two profile-card identifier edges; if a new surface needs a colour, it gets brass or it gets grey.
Do open every new section with a one-pixel hairline rule and pad it with the section spacing clamp.
Do separate a surface from the ground with a hairline plus the neutral wash at 20–26% alpha over graphite.
Do keep the neutrals neutral: new greys are sampled off the graphite ramp, not tinted.
Do set body copy in Poppins 300 and let emphasis reach only to weight 500 and Bone.
Do pick a radius by function: control radius for anything the user acts on, card radius for anything that holds content.
Do keep form inputs at 16px, interactive targets at 44px minimum, and functional text at or above 11.5px.

Do theme the browser's own surfaces on any new page — brass ::selection on graphite, brass caret-color, the thin brass scrollbar, the 2px Lit Brass :focus-visible ring at 3px offset, and a 4px underline offset on focused links.
Do draw chevrons, carets and arrows as CSS shapes or inline sprite SVG, keeping the page at zero third-party requests.
Do give new scroll-revealed content the reveal class and an explicit --i, and confirm it reads with motion disabled.
donts: Don't fill a button, a link, a stamp or a hover state with Pole Red or Pole Blue. They identify and they stripe the pole; they are not an accent pair for general use.
Don't repeat the pole. One bar, on the H1, once per page — not on section rules, not as a bullet, not as a divider. It was tried on section rules, read as a dashed grey line, and was removed.
Don't put a hue back into the neutrals, and don't reintroduce a navy ramp. The ground is neutral so that brass and the pole are the only chroma.
Don't put an eyebrow, kicker, ordinal or coloured rule above a section heading. The heading stands alone; ordinals belong to the four implantation steps only.
Don't fill a surface with a gradient. The three gradients in the system draw the pole, the 5px select caret and the photograph's scrim.
Don't add a shadow to a card, tile, input or list row, and don't use a shadow as a hover affordance. Shadows exist only as contact darkening under physically overlapping objects.
Don't add a second typeface, and don't set body copy above weight 300 or headings above 500.
Don't use icon fonts, glyph characters, emoji or a third-party icon package; extend the inline sprite instead.
Don't wrap a product screenshot in device chrome, a browser bar, a mockup bezel or a perspective transform. A hairline frame over Leather is the treatment.
Don't invent a third radius or a dashed stroke, and don't use a thick border for anything but the two profile-card identifier edges.
Don't animate anything twice, and don't add parallax, scale or directional slides — besides the pole, the reveal is a 14px rise with a fade.
